notes: rk-nsex Tier A repair wave, LANDING-BLOCKER BL3, THE LEGACY CONTROL — and the fixture that keeps the migration path honest in both directions. No `.rk/config.json` at all, so `records` resolves to its default `"legacy"`: the byte-identical tree that ERRORs in `refs-37` here draws WARN `[record-absent]` and the run exits 0. That is deliberate and it is a MIGRATION setting, not a resting state: every rk campaign predates extraction records, and turning every existing cited shard red on the day the check lands is how a gate gets switched off. What legacy does NOT do any more is hide the population — the coverage line reads `0/1 shard-record joins`, so the backlog is a number a campaign can watch go to zero before it flips `records: "required"`. The second shard (`lem-campaign`, `status: proved-mod-audit`, `origin: campaign`) proves the origin discriminator stays silent for a campaign's own proof in legacy mode and contributes nothing to the join denominator. `aism_behavior: n/a`. Mutation-proof: making the legacy branch ERROR turns this fixture red (verdict pass -> fail), which is the guard against a future change quietly removing the migration path; observed and reverted.
